List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Rescheduling of flights on account of
foggy conditions
*21. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
 Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a)  whether during December, 2006 and
January, 2007, dense fog enveloped the
Indira Gandhi International Airport and
night visibility dropped to zero, due to
which flights got disrupted and passengers
were stranded for hours as airline operators
failed to inform  the passengers on time
about the delays and rescheduling;
(b)  whether on personal inspection,
DGCA found that many trained pilots are
out of India on international  sectors and
many CAT III-B trained pilots are not even
in India in this foggy season; and
(c)  the steps taken or are likely to be
taken in future to avoid such situation?
 Illegal share transfer  from Demat
accounts
*22. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Demat
account holders in various banks are facing
loss of shares from their Demat accounts
through forged signatures;
(b)  if so, the action taken by
Government to control this practice and to
help the victims;
(c)  if not, whether Government intend
to bring measures to control the spread of
illegal share transfer from Demat account
holders, along with details thereof; and
(d)  the details of aggrieved persons till
now and the measures taken/proposed to
protect them?
 Profit earned by Navratna companies
†*23. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
 Will the Minister of HEAVY
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES  be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that the status of
'Navratna' has been given to several public
sector industries by Government in the
country;

9
(b)  if so, the names of those industries
and the average amount of money earned
as profit annually by each of those
industrial units during the last three years;
and
(c)  the percentage of this profit as
against the total capital invested in the
industrial units?
 Depletion of ground water
*24. SHRI DEVDAS APTE:  Will the
Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government are aware that
some private agencies/plants are exploiting
underground water that causes the
depletion of ground water level;
(b)  if so, the details thereof;
(c)  whether Government are
considering to impose fine or sanctions on
the cold drink plants that are engaged in the
depletion of ground water; and
(d)  if so, the details thereof?
Educational loans for students
†*25. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ:  Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government
have formulated a plan to provide bank
loans to students for studying abroad;
(b)  if so, the rate of interest to be
charged on this loan;
(c)  the number of students who applied
for this loan during the last two years;
(d)  the number of applications
approved alongwith the amount allocated;
and
(e)  the main reason for rejecting
applications?
 VRS in Public Sector Enterprises
*26. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
MS. MABEL REBELLO:
 Will the Minister of HEAVY
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:
(a)  the number of employees of CPSEs
who have opted for VRS during the last
three years, year-wise;
(b)  which are the PSEs where VRS
optees are maximum alongwith Ministry-
wise details thereof;
(c)  the number of VRS optees who
have been trained under Counselling,
Retraining and Redeployment (CRR)
Scheme including class C&D employees;
(d)  the number of CRR beneficiaries
who are actually redeployed;
(e)  whether it is a fact that the rate of
redeployment is insignificant as compared
to VRS optees; and
(f) the steps being taken to improve the
standard of training under CRR to make
trainees employable?
 Regulation and management of
Ground and River-water
*27. SHRI DARA SINGH:
SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
 Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government have so far
formulated any comprehensive National
Policy for regulation and management of
ground-water and river-water in the
country, initiated by the previous

Total number of questions — 130
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Expansion of Amritsar airport
†131. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that it is being
contemplated to expand Amritsar airport
with new technology;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) by when this work would be
completed; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Problems due to fog
†132. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDEL-
WAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that foggy
conditions in Delhi alone led to loss of more
than 18 crores of rupees in the first week
of January itself;
(b) whether it is also a fact that problem
of passengers have not yet lessened despite
installation of many modern equipments;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the arrangements being made by
Government for the passengers stranded
in the said situation at airports?
Airport at Sindhdurg
133. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Maharashtra with the Centre's help has
decided to set up an airport at Sindhdurg in
order to attract tourists;
(b) if so, whether the area is scenic and
there are beaches similar to Goa and the
airport will be located 25 Km from Kudal
city and will come up on 306 hectors; and
(c) if so, the total cost involved in this
project and by when this will be completed?
Leasing of planes by private airlines
134. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
some private airlines are taking planes on
32

33
lease from their own established companies
outside India to get subsidy;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have made any
special arrangement for looking after the
taking of lease by the private airlines; and
(d) if so, what is the report which has
been submitted during the last two years?
Communication between IGIA and
other airports
135. SHRI T. T. V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
air congestion which still continues at the
airports are resulting in wastage of aviation
fuel;
(b) whether it is a fact that in the age of
Internet, the communication between IGIA
and other airports is dependent on landline
telephones; and
(c) if so, the details of proposals with
Government to modernize the Air Traffic
Control of IGIA for communication with
the other airports to avoid the frequent
delays of flights?
New policy for internatinal cargo
136. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a panel has
been formed to script private cargo
companies which are ready to take off;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a new
policy is going to be developed for handling
international cargo; and
(d) if so, the salient features of this
policy?
Medical emergencies at airports
137. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the spate of deaths of air
passengers at the Mumbai and other airports
has prompted his Ministry to draft a
comprehensive action plan to tackle public
health emergencies in air or at the airport
and set up state-of-the-art emergency
medical services at major airports;
(b) whether his Ministry has drafted a
multi-pronged strategy for the purpose; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
FDI in civil aviation sector
138. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
allowing foreign direct investment up to 74
per cent in cargo operation, non-scheduled
airlines, helicopter and seaplane operations;
(b) if so, whether Government are keen
to attract FDI and are looking to open the
market although and have an overall FDI
cap of 49 per cent in the aviation sector;
and
(c) if so, by when a final decision for
allowing 74 per cent FDI in some sectors
of civil aviation will be taken?
FDI in Civil Aviation Sector
139. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
allow 100 per cent FDI for seaplanes,

maintenance and overhaul facilities for
charter and other non-scheduled operations;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government propose to
increase FDI for commercial airlines also
and if so, the details thereof and the reasons
therefor; and

propose to safeguard the interest of
